items.followUp: What is the difference between primary and secondary memory?

rubric.why: Identifies the kinds of information stored in memory.
rubric.description: States that memory stores data and instructions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning that memory stores data and instructions.

rubric.why: Explains memory's role in a computer.
rubric.description: Connects stored information with computer processing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that memory holds information for processing.

modelAnswer: Memory is the storage area of a computer in which data and instructions are stored.
The computer uses this stored information for processing.

items.followUp: Write the hexadecimal representation of the decimal number 31.

rubric.why: States the base or number of symbols used in hexadecimal.
rubric.description: Identifies hexadecimal as a base-16 number system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating its base is 16 or that it uses 16 symbols.

rubric.why: Gives the symbols used to represent hexadecimal numbers.
rubric.description: Names the digits 0–9 and letters A–F.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying both ranges of symbols.

modelAnswer: The hexadecimal number system is a base-16 number system.
It uses the symbols 0–9 and A–F to represent numbers.

items.followUp: State the output of an OR gate when both inputs are 0.

rubric.why: Describes when the OR operation produces 1.
rubric.description: States that the result is 1 if at least one input is 1.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the condition that one or more inputs are 1.

rubric.why: Describes the OR operation's zero-output condition.
rubric.description: States that the result is 0 only when all inputs are 0.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating the zero-output condition.

modelAnswer: The OR operator in Boolean algebra gives an output of 1 if any input is 1.
It gives an output of 0 only when all inputs are 0.

items.followUp: How many digits are used in the binary number system, and what are they?

rubric.why: Identifies the base of the binary system.
rubric.description: States that binary is a base-2 number system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that its base is 2.

rubric.why: Names the digits used in binary notation.
rubric.description: States that binary uses only 0 and 1.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both binary digits.

modelAnswer: The binary number system is a base-2 number system.
It uses only the digits 0 and 1.

rubric.why: Identifies copying without permission as piracy.
rubric.description: States that piracy involves unauthorized copying of software.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning copying without authorization.

rubric.why: Makes clear that the unauthorized act concerns protected software.
rubric.description: Connects piracy with software or copyrighted material.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the copied material as software or copyrighted material.

modelAnswer: Software piracy is the unauthorized copying of software.
It also includes using or distributing copyrighted software without permission.

items.followUp: Why is unauthorized access to a computer system a security risk?

rubric.why: Captures the defining feature of hacking in this context.
rubric.description: States that hacking involves gaining access without permission.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning access without authorization.

rubric.why: Identifies the target of the unauthorized access.
rubric.description: States that the unauthorized access is to a computer or network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a computer, computer system, or network as the target.

modelAnswer: Hacking is gaining unauthorized access to a computer system or network.
A hacker may access, alter, or misuse information without permission.

items.followUp: What is the function of the data link layer?

rubric.why: Identifies the type of information handled at this layer.
rubric.description: States that the physical layer deals with raw bits.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the transmission of bits.

rubric.why: Explains where or how the bits are transmitted.
rubric.description: States that the layer sends bits over a physical communication medium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the physical medium or communication channel.

modelAnswer: The physical layer is responsible for transmitting raw bits.
It sends these bits over the physical communication medium.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of HTTPS?

rubric.why: Identifies what HTTP stands for or its protocol role.
rubric.description: Names HTTP as Hypertext Transfer Protocol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly naming HTTP or identifying it as a transfer protocol.

rubric.why: Explains the web communication HTTP supports.
rubric.description: States that HTTP transfers web pages or data between a browser and a web server.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the transfer of web content or communication between browser and server.

modelAnswer: HTTP stands for Hypertext Transfer Protocol.
It is used to transfer web pages and other web data between a web browser and a web server.
